subject: Computer Studies
sourceFile: Copy of Basic Science & Tech BECE Syllabus - syllabusNG.txt
examFormat: The BECE Basic Science and Technology syllabus aims to help candidates gain a fundamental understanding of science and technology, apply scientific and technological knowledge to address modern societal needs, and be equipped with essential knowledge for further studies in science and technology. Basic Science and Technology is examined in four compulsory papers (I–IV). Computer Studies is examined in Paper II, which has 60 multiple-choice questions covering Basic Technology and Computer Studies with an allocated time of sixty minutes, and in Paper III, one Computer Studies practical question taken from an application package (such as CorelDraw, Paint, Instant Artist, Microsoft Word or a spreadsheet), to be finished in 45 minutes.
excluded: Syllabus.ng marketing ("About us", "About BECE"), eligibility, registration, grading table, table of contents and the FAQ chapter were left out. The Basic Science, Basic Technology and Physical and Health Education themes of the same file are in their own subject files.
recommendedTexts: Highway to Information Technology — S. G. Adedapo et al. (Rasmed Publications, Ibadan)
Computer Studies for Junior Secondary School 1–3 — Wole Olatokun, Rosemary Agbonlahor, Sunday Adeniran et al. (HEBN Publishers PLC)

topics.name: Historical Development of Computers
topics.content: Sub-theme: Basic computer operations and concepts.

subtopics.name: Early counting devices
objectives: Identify early counting devices: cowries, fingers, stones, sticks, pebbles, etc.

subtopics.name: Mechanical counting and calculating devices
objectives: Identify mechanical counting and calculating devices such as the abacus and slide rule.

subtopics.name: Electro-mechanical counting devices
objectives: Describe electro-mechanical counting devices: John Napier's bones, Blaise Pascal's machine, Gottfried Leibniz's machine, Joseph Jacquard's loom, Charles Babbage's analytical machine, and the work of Philip Emeagwali.

subtopics.name: Electronic counting devices and modern computers
objectives: Describe electronic counting devices and modern computers: Herman Hollerith's punch cards and John Von Neumann's machine.

subtopics.name: Generations of computers
objectives: Describe the generations of computers from the first to the fifth.

topics.name: Data Processing
topics.content: Sub-theme: Basic computer operations and concepts.

subtopics.name: Definition of data and data processing
objectives: Define data and data processing.

subtopics.name: Data processing cycle
objectives: Describe the data processing cycle: data gathering, data collation, input stage, processing stage, storage stage and output stage.

subtopics.name: Importance of the computer in data processing
objectives: State the importance of the computer as a tool for processing data: increased accuracy, efficient storage facilities, fast access to information and handling repetitive tasks.

topics.name: Computer Ethics
topics.content: Sub-theme: Basic computer operations and concepts.

subtopics.name: Computer room management ethics
objectives: Describe computer room management ethics: maintaining a dust-free environment, appropriate ventilation, and appropriate lighting system and computer setting.

subtopics.name: Laboratory rules and regulations
objectives: Apply laboratory rules and regulations: arranging chairs and tables in a comfortable manner and arranging computers and their peripherals in an orderly manner.

subtopics.name: Responsible use of computers and the internet
objectives: Describe responsible use of computers and the internet: preventing liquid dropping into the system, using a dust cover, protection from power problems, unplugging the system when not in use for long, checking e-mail regularly and responding to mails promptly and politely.

subtopics.name: Abuse and misuse of computers
objectives: Explain the abuse/misuse of computers.

topics.name: Computer Viruses
topics.content: Sub-theme: Basic computer operations and concepts.

subtopics.name: Meaning of computer virus

subtopics.name: Types of computer virus
objectives: Identify types of computer virus: boot sector, executable file virus and attack on documents.

subtopics.name: Examples of viruses
objectives: Give examples of viruses: Trojan horse, sleeper, logic bomb, Alabama virus, Christmas virus.

subtopics.name: Sources of viruses
objectives: Identify sources of viruses: infected diskettes, infected CD-ROMs, e-mails, internet downloads, illegal duplication of software, etc.

subtopics.name: Virus warning signs
objectives: Identify virus warning signs: slowing down of response time, tiny dots wandering across the screen, incomplete saving of a file, corruption of the system set-up instructions and appearance of strange characters.

subtopics.name: Virus detection (anti-virus)
objectives: Identify anti-virus programs: Norton Anti-Virus, McAfee VirusScan, Dr Solomon's Toolkit, etc.
